themes.summary: Safety work is turning into standing practice inside the labs: OpenAI now runs probes, a model reviewer and investigative agents over every RL run and eval of its top models, Anthropic has Claude assess each of its own conversations for misuse right after replying, and outside audits, behaviour reports and post-mortems like the one on Claude Mythos 5 are becoming routine. Studies of human oversight show the risk is real, with expert analysts following an agent's hidden lean 86% of the time. The stack around the models has become part of the attack surface too, from the OpenCode breach and an SGLang cache bug that leaked other users' output to a tampered Claude Code extension that sat in Cursor's marketplace for about 11 hours.
themes.title: Safety, security and provenance go operational

themes.summary: Agents are moving from single chats to long jobs: parallel agents in ChatGPT Pro, Gemini agents playing Minecraft for 27 hours, durable pi agents and dedicated memory models, and now GitHub rebuilding Copilot around parallel agent sessions that span repos and route each task across models. Engineering write-ups focus on the harness around the model: Meta split one overloaded agent into a router and 14 specialists, Ramp and LangChain built their own agent platforms, Cursor's Agent SDK packages agents as versioned code with evals, and Mistral offers a stateful Responses API. The hard problems are now state, memory, orchestration and testing.
themes.title: Agents become long-running, parallel and stateful

themes.summary: Mistral Large 4, now shipped as roughly 1T-parameter open weights tuned for coding agents, Meta's Muse Spark Open, Reflection's Beam and Moonshot's 2.8T-parameter Kimi K3.1 Pro have put frontier-scale models under open licences within a few weeks, and MiniMax's open-weight M3.1 Flash topped OpenCode before it was even named. Vercel's gateway data shows open weights already carry most production tokens, and Meta and DeepSeek have published recipes and engines for running them cheaply. Self-hosting is now a real alternative to paid APIs for coding and agent work.
themes.title: Open-weight models reach the frontier

themes.summary: The closed labs kept shipping: GPT-6 Sol, Luna and 6.1 Sol, Claude Haiku 5.5, Gemini 4 Argon, Meta's Muse Wonder and now Google DeepMind's Gemini 4 Carbon, which tops Artificial Analysis's new Index v5. OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Terra matches GPT-6 Astra on computer use at a tenth the price and over 3x the speed, aimed at high-volume agents. The competition is shifting toward speed, price tiers and agent workloads, and leaderboards are moving tests to private sets to keep rankings meaningful.
themes.title: Closed labs ship new flagships and faster tiers

themes.summary: Labs are pointing frontier models at research: OpenAI published new maths results and opened GPT-Rosalind to academic labs, Claude designed quantum circuits, a $15M fund backs AI in maths, and Anthropic started drug discovery of its own. The claims are now big enough to need formal review: physicists led by David Gross are vetting an AI result on Yang-Mills theory, and OpenAI and Anthropic models each claim a Lean-checked refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis that leading complexity theorists are reviewing in the open. Research results are becoming both a way labs show capability and a business line.
themes.title: AI turns to maths and science research

themes.summary: Agents now write code faster than Git hosting and review were built for. GitHub moved almost every repository to Azure under agent-driven load, Anthropic built its own source control after merges grew more than tenfold, and agent hours now outnumber staff hours six to one, leaving human review as the bottleneck. Teams are answering with automation: Cloudflare cut its per-review cost by 68% after it doubled, and Meta now has LLMs write just-in-time tests for every diff, catching 74 serious privacy bugs before they landed. Tooling built for human pace is giving way first.
themes.title: Infrastructure strains under agent-scale code

items.title: Anthropic files its S-1 for an IPO on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT
Anthropic hands Agent Skills to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation
Anthropic commits 5% of its shares to a new Public Benefit Fund

themes.summary: Anthropic filed an S-1 to list on Nasdaq as ANT, a week after committing 5% of its shares to a Public Benefit Fund that, with staff pledges, puts about 20% of its equity toward public benefit. It also handed its Agent Skills standard to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation, as it did with MCP. A frontier lab going public puts its finances and governance in the open and sets a template for how safety-focused labs raise capital.
themes.title: Anthropic reshapes its governance on the way to an IPO

themes.summary: Always-on personal agents went from demos to products this month. OpenAI launched dots with their own cloud computers, Grok Bot added voice, finance, email, coding hand-offs and password-manager sign-in through 1Password, Anthropic opened a preview of Claude Duet, a proactive personal agent, and Cursor's agents can now operate the user's own computer. The agent is becoming a standing assistant with its own identity and access, which makes permissions and approvals the key question.
themes.title: Personal agents get their own computers, accounts and money

themes.summary: As agents run code and touch production, containment is getting real engineering. Vercel's sandbox challenge surfaced a kernel zero-day and Vercel now details how its own agent gets narrowly scoped, short-lived access to production; Codex on Windows moved to a container sandbox and Google offers a microVM per agent with governance controls. Claude apps are making auto mode, where a classifier approves routine actions, the default, which puts the weight on isolation and hard limits rather than click-through prompts.
themes.title: Sandboxes and limits for agents that act

themes.summary: Assistants are spreading into existing work surfaces: Claude inside Google Docs, Sheets and Slides, live dashboards in Claude, voice upgrades in ChatGPT, and Cursor bundled into an X subscription. Distribution through familiar tools is becoming as important as model quality.
themes.title: Assistants move into the tools people already use
